subject: Post-demo: p95/p99 latency + streaming acceptance — next steps and observable checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@clarityhealth.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: p95/p99 latency + streaming acceptance — next steps and observable checklist

Thanks again for the time this morning, Sam — great conversation and very helpful signal on production traffic shape. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps.

Summary of what we heard (from Clarify):
- Primary inference route: clinical-annotation endpoint (single-shot text-in -> structured-out).
- Peak sustained traffic expected for PoC: ~40 RPS, short bursts to 70 RPS for 2–3 minutes.
- Streaming preview use-case: clinician session transcripts; concurrent streaming sessions estimated at 15–20 during peak clinic hours.
- Quality expectation: p95 end-to-end (client -> Redwood hosted API -> model -> client) target ~200 ms, p99 target ~650 ms for the single-shot route.

Open technical questions we’ll action in the PoC:
1) Exact request/response size distribution: we asked for a sample traffic CSV (attached) — confirms median prompt ~450 tokens, 95th ~1,100 tokens.
2) Concurrency model for streaming: whether sessions are long-lived (minutes) or short chunks — this affects KV cache residency and batching.
3) Failure/fallback policy expectations: hard vs soft latency SLOs and whether Clarify wants automatic model-fallback or region fallback on sustained tail events.

Immediate next steps and owners:
- Clarify: confirm the streaming session length distribution and share one week of anonymized traffic (Sam) — due EOD Wed, Apr 18.
- Redwood SE (Ben): propose shadow-run matrix (traffic profile, concurrency slices, and sampling hooks) by Tue, Apr 18.
- Redwood Sales (Marissa): share commercial PoC terms and PO contact; align on NDA/procurement cadence.
- Karthik: schedule two 90-minute windows for a shadow run (we suggested Apr 24 morning and Apr 26 afternoon) — calendar invite to follow.

Observability / acceptance checklist we will validate during PoC:
- Token-level latency distribution (client -> ingress -> egress) with p50/p95/p99 slices.
- Per-route KV cache hit/miss metrics and batching rates.
- End-to-end tracing (sampled spans) to map where tail is incurred.
- Streaming stall events and per-chunk latency.
- Cost-per-1k tokens baseline for the test traffic.

Attachments: clarity-demo-traffic-envelope.csv (sample traffic), redwood-slo-proposal-v1.pdf (PoC acceptance criteria draft). Drive folder with runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-clarity-demo

If the targets above (200ms p95 / 650ms p99) are off the mark, flag now — it changes the PoC shape (quantization, batching aggressiveness, and node sizing).

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0129

Cc: procurement@clarityhealth.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: p95/p99 latency + streaming acceptance — next steps and observable checklist

Thanks for the thorough recap, Karthik — that aligns with what we discussed on the call. A few clarifications from our side:
- The clinical-annotation endpoint is the highest priority for latency; we expect median requests around 400–500 tokens, but occasionally larger operational notes up to ~1,500 tokens (rare).
- Confirming the targets we asked to validate: p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 650 ms for single-shot responses under the stated traffic envelope (40 RPS sustained, 70 RPS burst).
- Streaming: typical clinician sessions are ~6–10 minutes; each session streams short chunks (~200–400 tokens) every 10–20 seconds. Concurrent streaming peaks ~18 sessions.
- Fallbacks: we prefer a soft-fail policy for PoC (return 503 after 5s and retry client-side) but would like Redwood to propose an automated fallback plan (lower-capacity quantized model or degraded feature set) if sustained p99 violations occur.

I’ve looped in procurement for commercial coordination. I’ll try to get the anonymized traffic extract to you by Wednesday; if there’s anything specific you need in that CSV (headers or fields), let me know.

—Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Engineering, Clarity Health
sam@clarityhealth.ai | +1 650-555-0921
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@clarityhealth.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: p95/p99 latency + streaming acceptance — next steps and observable checklist

Appreciate the quick confirm, Sam — this is actionable. I’ll own the engineering side for the PoC. Proposed immediate plan:

1) Shadow-run matrix (deliverable: detailed runbook + measurement dashboard) — Ben (owner)
   - Traffic slices: 10/25/40/70 RPS sustained, 70 RPS 3-minute burst test.
   - Payload sizes: median, 95th (1,100 tokens), and the rare large ones (~1,500 tokens).
   - Streaming concurrency: 5/12/18 concurrent sessions.
   - Acceptance gates: measured p95/p99 for single-shot route; streaming per-chunk p95 and session-level stall rate.

2) Observability hooks (we’ll add these before the run):
   - End-to-end request-id tracing, token-level latency histograms, KV cache hit rate, batching factor, and server-side retry counts.
   - We’ll provide a Grafana snapshot and a link to a temporary dashboard during the run.

3) Fallback proposals:
   - Auto-fallback to a quantized model (reduced quality) as first-tier, and region-failover as second-tier. We’ll simulate both during the run and measure the quality delta.

4) Schedule and logistics:
   - Proposed shadow-run windows: Apr 24, 09:00–10:30 PT (preferred) OR Apr 26, 15:00–16:30 PT (backup). Please confirm which works for your ops team.
   - Estimated engineer time: 2 SEs from Redwood for test execution and 1 SRE to monitor; we’ll forward a final calendar invite once Sam confirms the window.

Commercial / procurement items (Marissa): please coordinate NDA/PO and confirm whether Clarify prefers a simple PoC MSA or a short-term SOW. We’ll need PO contact details to expedite.

I attached the proposed SLO checklist (redwood-slo-proposal-v1.pdf) — it’s intentionally conservative; we can tighten thresholds if the traffic extract indicates smaller tail behavior.

Next immediate asks: Sam — can you confirm the Apr 24 slot and send the traffic extract? If you can’t get the full week, even a 24–48 hour slice with client timestamps and token counts will be enough to tune the run.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0188
